title: Synthetic: linear recurrence a(n) = 1 a(n-1) + 1 a(n-2) + 1 a(n-3) (mod 2^64), naive vs DP vs matrix power
problem_statement: Given n >= 0, compute a(n) mod 2^64 where a(n) = 1 a(n-1) + 1 a(n-2) + 1 a(n-3) for n >= 3 and a(0..2) = (0, 0, 1).

input.parameter: n, the index (a value, not a length).
input.size_measure: Complexities are stated in the VALUE n; in binary the input has about log2(n) bits (see caveats).

algorithms.name: naive recursion (deliberately wasteful)
algorithms.idea: Transcribe the recurrence directly; overlapping subterms are recomputed.
algorithms.pseudocode: a(n) = sum over i with c_i != 0 of c_i * a(n-i), recursively
algorithms.time_complexity: Theta(lambda^n) calls, lambda = 1.8392867552 (largest real root of x^3 = x^2 + x + 1)
algorithms.correctness: Direct transcription. Call count C(n) = 1 + sum_{i in S} C(n-i), whose growth rate is the dominant root lambda of the characteristic polynomial of the support S.

algorithms.name: bottom-up dynamic programming
algorithms.idea: Keep a sliding window of the last k values.
algorithms.pseudocode: window = a(0..k-1); repeat: append sum c_i * window[-i]
algorithms.correctness: Loop invariant: the window holds a(m-k), ..., a(m-1).

algorithms.name: companion-matrix power
algorithms.idea: The state vector advances by the companion matrix; raise it to the power n - k + 1 by squaring.
algorithms.correctness: (a(m), ..., a(m-k+1))^T = C (a(m-1), ..., a(m-k))^T for the companion matrix C.

relationship: Same idea as pairs/fibonacci-naive-vs-dp, generated mechanically: exponential naive recursion -> linear DP -> logarithmic matrix power.

sources.title: The Art of Computer Programming, Vol. 1: Fundamental Algorithms (3rd ed.)

verification.method: Generated by generators/linear_recurrence.py; checked by tools/validate.py: V1 checks agreement of the three algorithms (naive up to n = 20) and the initial values; V2 fits wall-clock times against lambda^n, n and log n (timing data, conclusive only up to log factors; no rival costs declared). lambda is computed by bisection (200 iterations) and rounded to 10 decimals in the cost expression.

caveats: T7 SYNTHETIC: the slow algorithm is a deliberately naive transcription; low signal (START_HERE section 5); never counted as a validated pair. Bit-size view as in the Fibonacci entry: the DP is exponential in log n; only the matrix power is polynomial in the input length. No independent oracle beyond the initial values.
